note: A small vetted list of MCP servers (phase 4 step 5). Each entry names the official package or endpoint, what it needs, and the leash domain Maka proposes per tool. Nothing here is a secret: secret values are typed once when the server is added and go to the keystore. `{param}` in args is filled from the params; `$SECRET:NAME` in args is filled from the keystore when the server starts.

entries.label: Filesystem
entries.description: Read, search and write files under one directory you name. The reference server from the MCP project.

params.name: path
params.label: Directory the server may access
params.hint: Pick a directory outside your Rangers' workspaces only if they should write there; every write still passes the leash.

params.name: version
params.label: Package version
params.hint: Pin a version once you have tested one.

entries.notes: Writes fall under publishing (a file appears or changes on this machine); moving a file can remove it from where it was, so it is data_deletion.

entries.label: GitHub
entries.description: Repositories, issues, pull requests and code search with a personal access token. The reference server from the MCP project.

secrets.name: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
secrets.label: GitHub personal access token
secrets.hint: A fine-grained token scoped to the repositories the Rangers may touch.

entries.notes: Public writes (files, issues, pull requests, comments) are publishing; a new repository or a fork is account_creation.

entries.label: Google Drive
entries.description: Search and read files in a Google Drive. The reference server from the MCP project; it needs a Google Cloud OAuth client and a one-time sign-in run outside Maka.

params.name: credentialsPath
params.label: Path of the saved Google credentials file
params.hint: Produced by the server's own `auth` step (see its README); the file stays on this machine.

entries.notes: Read-only: files are read as resources. The credentials file is yours to protect; Maka never copies it.

entries.label: Notion
entries.description: Notion's own hosted MCP server over streamable HTTP; sign in with OAuth from the Peak after adding it.
entries.notes: Notion's server names its read tools read-only, so they land in research by default; every other tool is outbound_messages until you map it. The sign-in is a Gate item.

entries.label: Slack (workspace tools)
entries.description: Post and read in Slack channels with a bot token. The reference server from the MCP project. Distinct from Maka's own Slack owner channel.

secrets.name: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
secrets.label: Slack bot token (xoxb-…)
secrets.hint: A bot token for the workspace the Rangers may post in; not the token Maka's owner channel uses.

entries.notes: Posting is outbound_messages (the default); the reads are mapped to research explicitly because the reference server carries no read-only hints.

entries.label: Postgres (read-only)
entries.description: Run read-only SQL against one database. The reference server from the MCP project; it opens READ ONLY transactions.

secrets.name: DATABASE_URL
secrets.label: Connection URL (postgresql://user:password@host/db)
secrets.hint: Use a read-only role. The URL carries the password, so it lives in the keystore and is handed to the server as an argument only when it starts.

entries.notes: The server itself refuses writes (read-only transactions); `query` is mapped to research for that reason.

entries.label: Brave Search
entries.description: Web and local search through the Brave Search API. The reference server from the MCP project.

secrets.name: BRAVE_API_KEY
secrets.label: Brave Search API key
secrets.hint: The same key the Scout's web.search can use (BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY); this server is an alternative, not a requirement.

entries.notes: Read-only lookups of public results: research.
